mnemonic: 바람 = a gust of wind: something sudden knocks your plans over, and the damage is already done.
meaning: because of a sudden, unexpected event, with an unwanted result ("…, and so I ended up …")
nuance: The cause is typically a sudden or unforeseen event, and its (usually unwanted) result has already happened. The modifier stays -는 even for past events: 넘어지는 바람에 (넘어진 바람에 is nonstandard). The main clause is normally past tense and cannot be a command or suggestion (-(으)세요, -자, -(으)ㅂ시다). The tone is neutral: it reports what happened without blaming anyone or describing the atmosphere.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 points a finger: the cause is held responsible. -는 바람에 just reports a sudden cause.
-는 통에 blames a hectic, chaotic scene (noise, crowds, commotion); -는 바람에 is typically a single sudden event.

mnemonic: 탓 = fault, as in "네 탓이야!" The clause is the finger you point at the cause.
meaning: because of (a cause blamed for a bad outcome); "owing to", "thanks to" in the sarcastic sense

mnemonic: 뿐 'only' + 더러 'what's more': not only that, there's more, all in one word.
meaning: not only … but also; on top of that (adds a second point pulling the same way)
nuance: Adds a second fact in the same evaluative direction as the first: both points for, or both against. It is a single ending, so it is written attached (쌀뿐더러, not 쌀 뿐더러); compare -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라, where 뿐 is a separate word and is spaced. contrasts.note: -거니와 does the same additive job but sounds literary, and it also has a set discourse use (다시 말하거니와).
-(으)ㄴ/는 데다가 is the everyday spoken workhorse for piling up facts; -(으)ㄹ뿐더러 is a notch more formal.
-기는커녕 reverses direction: the expected thing didn't happen at all.

mnemonic: Picture an orator raising a finger: '…and furthermore, I say again…' That's 거니와.

mnemonic: It's the sturdier cousin of -아/어도: 도 is still the 'even' at the end.
meaning: even if; even though (concession, often hypothetical)
nuance: A firmer, more deliberate 'even if' than -아/어도, typically for a hypothetical or for a fact the speaker concedes. The main clause can be almost anything: a statement, a resolution (-겠다), advice, a command, or a suggestion. That flexibility is what sets it apart from -(으)ㄹ망정 and -(으)ㄹ지언정, which state the speaker's own stance.

-(으)ㄹ지언정 is the emphatic, literary 'even if …, never …'.

mnemonic: Same 망정 as in -기에 망정이지 ('good thing that…'): in a bad scenario, find the one thing to hold on to.
meaning: (1) even if it means …, (I won't) …; (2) although …, at least …

cloze.sentence: 먼 길을 {{}} 그 사람 차는 절대 안 탈 거야.

nearMiss.hint: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: 걸을망정.

cloze.sentence: 당장 표를 {{}} 원칙을 저버리는 공약은 내놓지 않겠습니다.
cloze.en: We may lose votes in the short term, but we will not put forward pledges that betray our principles.

nuance.situation: 친구가 새로 구한 원룸이 너무 좁다고 속상해해요. 위로하려면? (Your friend is upset that their new studio is tiny. You cheer them up.)

options.text: 방은 좁을망정 햇볕은 잘 들잖아.
options.why: Concede the drawback, then point to the redeeming fact: use (2) of -(으)ㄹ망정.

options.text: 방은 좁을망정 햇볕도 안 들잖아.
options.why: The second clause has to be the consolation. Adding more bad news with 도 turns it into a pile-on, which -(으)ㄹ망정 can't do.

options.text: 방이 좁은 바람에 햇볕은 잘 들잖아.
options.why: -는 바람에 needs a sudden event causing an unwanted result; a small room doesn't cause good sunlight (and the form would be -는).

nuance.situation: 처음 차린 가게가 작은 구멍가게지만 내 가게라서 뿌듯해요. (Your first shop is just a tiny corner store, but it's yours and you're proud of it.)

options.text: 작은 구멍가게일망정 내 가게라서 뿌듯해.
options.why: Concede the drawback, then the redeeming fact: use (2) of -(으)ㄹ망정, attached to the copula as 일망정.

options.text: 작은 구멍가게인 망정 내 가게라서 뿌듯해.
options.why: 망정 here is part of the ending -(으)ㄹ망정, so the copula takes -ㄹ and attaches: 구멍가게일망정.

options.text: 작은 구멍가게인 덕분에 내 가게라서 뿌듯해.
options.why: 덕분에 makes the shop's smallness the cause of your pride; it doesn't concede a drawback.

mnemonic: Picture someone planting their feet: 지언정, not one step further, whatever it costs.
meaning: even if …, (I will) never …; would sooner … than …
nuance: An emphatic, somewhat literary concession: the speaker accepts the first (bad) scenario and flatly rules out the second. The main clause is typically a refusal or negation (-지 않겠다, 못 하다, -(으)ㄹ 수 없다), often reinforced by 차라리 in the first clause. Like -(으)ㄹ망정, it can also concede a past fact before a redeeming point (졌을지언정 정신력만큼은 뒤지지 않았다). At home in speeches, op-eds, and dramatic declarations.

contrasts.note: Near-synonym in both uses; -(으)ㄹ망정 is a little less emphatic and more conversational.
The same choice seen from the other side: -느니 attaches to the option rejected, -(으)ㄹ지언정 to the hardship accepted.

examples.ko: 차라리 굶을지언정 남의 도움은 받지 않겠다던 할아버지의 고집은 끝내 꺾이지 않았다.
examples.en: Grandfather, who'd said he'd sooner go hungry than accept help, never gave an inch.

examples.ko: 그는 질지언정 비겁한 방법은 쓰지 않는 선수였다.
examples.en: He was the kind of player who'd rather lose than win dirty.

cloze.sentence: 차라리 혼자 {{}} 마음 안 맞는 사람과는 일하고 싶지 않아.
cloze.en: I'd sooner work alone than work with someone I don't get along with.

nearMiss.hint: Also possible here; the cue asks for the more emphatic -(으)ㄹ지언정.
-느니 attaches to the option you reject; here working alone is the one you accept.

cloze.sentence: 평생 혼자 {{}} 마음에 없는 결혼은 하지 않겠다.
cloze.en: I'd sooner live alone all my life than marry someone I don't love.

nearMiss.hint: An ㄹ-stem takes plain -ㄹ: 살지언정.

cloze.sentence: 차라리 {{}} 그런 사람들과 어울리고 싶지는 않다.
cloze.en: I'd rather be lonely than hang around with people like that.

nearMiss.hint: 외롭다 is ㅂ-irregular: 외로울지언정.

cloze.sentence: 차라리 싫은 소리를 {{}} 거짓말로 둘러대지는 않겠다.
cloze.en: I'd rather take a scolding than talk my way out with a lie.

nearMiss.hint: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 들을지언정.

cloze.sentence: 평생 {{}} 남의 작품을 베끼는 일은 하지 않겠다.
cloze.en: I'd sooner stay unknown my whole life than copy someone else's work.

cloze.sentence: 그날 경기에서는 {{}} 정신력만큼은 상대에게 뒤지지 않았다.
cloze.en: We may have lost that day, but in mental toughness we were every bit our opponents' equal.

nearMiss.hint: That match is over: 졌을지언정.

cloze.sentence: 집을 작게 {{}} 빚을 내서 무리하고 싶지는 않아요.
cloze.en: I'd rather build a smaller house than take on debt and overextend myself.

nearMiss.hint: 짓다 is ㅅ-irregular: 지을지언정.

cloze.sentence: 회사가 손해를 {{}} 고객 정보를 팔아넘기는 일은 없을 것입니다.
cloze.en: Even if the company takes a loss, it will not sell off customer data.

nearMiss.hint: -느니 marks the option you reject; taking a loss is the hardship accepted, so it takes -(으)ㄹ지언정.

cloze.sentence: 차라리 밤을 {{}} 내일 아침에 허둥대고 싶지는 않아.
cloze.en: I'd rather pull an all-nighter than be scrambling tomorrow morning.

nearMiss.hint: Also possible; the cue asks for the more emphatic -(으)ㄹ지언정.

nuance.situation: 원칙을 지키는 기자가 사표를 쓰는 한이 있어도 기사를 고치지는 않겠다는 뜻을 밝히려고 해요. (A principled reporter vows she'll resign before she alters her story.)

options.text: 사표를 쓸지언정 기사를 고치지는 않겠습니다.
options.why: The hardship accepted (resigning) takes -(으)ㄹ지언정; the act refused follows, negated.

options.text: 기사를 고칠지언정 사표는 쓰지 않겠습니다.
options.why: Grammatical, but it says the opposite: she'd alter the story rather than resign.

options.text: 사표를 쓸지언정 기사를 고치겠습니다.
options.why: After -(으)ㄹ지언정 the main clause should rule something out; 'even if I resign, I'll alter it' doesn't hang together.

nuance.situation: 친구가 모임에 늦을 것 같다고 해요. 늦어도 괜찮으니 꼭 오라고 하려면? (A friend says they may be late to the get-together. You tell them to come anyway.)

options.text: 좀 늦더라도 꼭 와.
options.why: -더라도 concedes the lateness and can lead into a request.

options.text: 좀 늦을지언정 꼭 와.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ지언정 sets up a hardship the speaker accepts while ruling something out. Its main clause is a refusal or negation, not a request.

options.text: 좀 늦는 바람에 꼭 와.
options.why: -는 바람에 reports a sudden cause of something that already happened; it can't concede, and no request can follow it.

register.source: 회사를 그만둘지언정 부당한 지시는 따르지 않을 거야.
accepted: 회사를 그만둘지언정 부당한 지시는 따르지 않겠습니다.

accepted: 나는 해고를 당할지언정 장부를 조작하지는 않을 거야.
나는 해고를 당할지언정 장부를 조작하지는 않겠어.
난 해고를 당할지언정 장부를 조작하지는 않을 거야.
난 해고를 당할지언정 장부를 조작하지는 않겠어.

mnemonic: 커녕 slams the door on the expectation: 'Praise? Far from it.'
meaning: far from …; let alone … (the expected thing didn't happen, and often the opposite did)
nuance: Emphatically denies the first, expected or hoped-for situation. The second clause either goes further in the same negative direction, often with 도/조차 + a negative (인사는커녕 쳐다보지도 않았다), or reports the opposite, often with 오히려/도리어 (칭찬하기는커녕 오히려 화를 냈다). Common in speech and writing, and frequently tinged with indignation.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 데다가 adds a fact that did happen; -기는커녕 denies the first fact outright.
Same contrast: -(으)ㄹ뿐더러 affirms both points.

examples.ko: 월급이 오르기는커녕 수당까지 줄었다.
examples.en: Far from getting a raise, I even had my allowances cut.

examples.ko: 걔는 고맙다는 말은커녕 연락 한 통 없더라.
examples.en: Forget a thank-you: I didn't hear a word from him.

cloze.sentence: 사과를 {{}} 오히려 내가 한소리를 들었다.
cloze.en: Far from getting an apology, I was the one who got told off.

nearMiss.hint: -(으)ㄴ/는 데다가 adds a fact that happened; the apology never came, so the cue asks for -기는커녕.

cloze.sentence: 택시를 탔는데 길이 막혀서 시간을 {{}} 오히려 더 늦었다.
cloze.en: I took a cab, but the traffic was so bad that, far from saving time, I got there even later.

cloze.sentence: 축하 {{}} 내 생일인 줄도 모르더라.
cloze.en: Forget birthday wishes. He didn't even know it was my birthday.

nearMiss.hint: 인사 ends in a vowel, so it takes 는: 인사는커녕.

cloze.sentence: 규제 완화 이후 집값이 {{}} 오히려 큰 폭으로 올랐다.
cloze.en: Since deregulation, far from stabilizing, housing prices have risen sharply.

cloze.sentence: 주말에 푹 {{}} 밀린 집안일 하느라 더 피곤해.
cloze.en: Far from resting up over the weekend, I'm even more tired from catching up on chores.

cloze.sentence: 그 논문은 기존 이론을 {{}} 오히려 그 이론을 뒷받침하는 결과를 내놓았다.

cloze.sentence: 새로 산 패딩은 {{}} 바람이 숭숭 들어온다.

cloze.sentence: 회사 측은 피해자에게 {{}} 책임을 회피하는 데만 급급했습니다.

nearMiss.hint: -(으)ㄴ/는 데다가 affirms the apology; it never came, so the cue asks for -기는커녕.

cloze.sentence: 그 약을 먹고 증상이 {{}} 더 심해졌어요.
cloze.en: Far from getting better after that medicine, my symptoms got worse.

nuance.situation: 올해 연봉 협상 결과를 동료에게 전하려고 해요. 기대와 달리 결과가 나빴어요. (Contrary to your hopes, this year's pay talks went badly.)

options.text: 연봉이 오르기는커녕 오히려 깎였어.
options.why: The hoped-for raise is denied and the opposite happened: textbook -기는커녕 + 오히려.

options.text: 연봉이 오르기는커녕 보너스까지 받았어.
options.why: After -기는커녕 the second clause must run against the hope; a bonus on top is good news, which contradicts the frame.

options.text: 연봉이 오른 데다가 오히려 깎였어.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 데다가 affirms the raise and then says it was cut: a contradiction.

nuance.situation: 소개팅 상대가 대화 내내 휴대폰만 봤다고 친구에게 말하려고 해요. (Your blind date spent the whole time on their phone. You tell a friend.)

options.text: 대화는커녕 눈도 제대로 안 마주치더라.
options.why: N은/는커녕 denies the expected thing and the second clause goes further in the negative direction.

options.text: 대화는커녕 이야기를 많이 나눴어.
options.why: After 커녕 the second clause has to go further in the negative direction. Chatting a lot contradicts it.

options.text: 대화하는 데다가 눈도 제대로 안 마주치더라.
options.why: -는 데다가 affirms that you talked and then adds a complaint, which doesn't hang together.
